public_rationale: The May 2022 evaluation of GPT-J and two GPT-Neo sizes found arithmetic errors and performance linked to training-term frequency [e1]. The July 2022 study of 7-billion- and 70-billion-parameter models found weaker performance on unrealistic or abstract content across three logical reasoning tasks [e2]. These results support recurring elementary errors and difficulty applying rules across different content in the tested models and settings [e1, e2]. The latter study also reported above-chance performance and error patterns similar to humans; it does not establish a complete absence of abstraction [e2].
limitations: The studies do not provide a population-wide percentage of LLMs with abstraction problems [e1, e2].
Training-frequency correlations do not by themselves establish the mechanism behind the errors [e1].
The reasoning study does not establish that these difficulties are unique to language models [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models still make silly errors, and problems of abstraction are widespread in them.

statement.excerpt: Silly errors certainly do, and problems of abstraction are widespread in large language models.
statement.document_title: Happy Groundhog Day, The AI Edition

our_interpretation: Silly errors means objectively incorrect answers on elementary tasks, such as arithmetic, rather than stylistic disagreements.
Abstraction means applying a rule or relation beyond familiar examples or content.
Widespread means recurring across multiple contemporary models and tasks, not that every model fails every test.
Use evaluations from the latest completed research year, 2022, and the pre-post portion of 2023 to assess the ongoing state.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary controlled evaluations document elementary errors and recurring failures to apply rules across multiple models, model sizes or task settings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations establish reliable elementary accuracy and robust rule transfer, with the alleged abstraction problems confined to isolated or invalid examples.

evidence.locator: Section 4, Summary; arithmetic and operation-inference results
evidence.explanation: Experiments on GPT-J and two GPT-Neo sizes find errors in arithmetic and strong dependence on training-term frequency. That supports elementary errors and fragile transfer, although frequency dependence alone does not prove an absence of reasoning.

The study tests 7-billion- and 70-billion-parameter models on three reasoning tasks and finds sensitivity to whether content is familiar or abstract. It also finds above-chance ability and similarities to human errors, which qualify any inference that the models cannot abstract at all.
